fields.sample_size: three purposively selected case studies (Apsaalooke/Crow, Anishinaabe, Hoopa Valley), chosen from a literature review (PubMed, Web of Science, National Indian Law Library, NCAI Tribal Public Health Law database) and a review of primary documents (laws, ordinances, scientific reports); no respondent sample
fields.study_design: qualitative multiple-case analysis of documents and secondary sources, categorised with Nutbeam's functional/interactive/critical literacy typology
fields.effect_estimate: Each case illustrates one literacy level in tribal water-quality contexts: Apsaalooke (functional EHL: accessible information and skills), Anishinaabe (interactive EHL), Hoopa Valley (critical EHL; the tribal ordinance and the circumstances of its development). Findings: community partnerships, skill-building and collaborative action matter, and communities and professionals face challenges in clarifying scientific findings, respecting cultural practices and translating policies and laws. Qualitative; no effect estimate.
fields.section: Full text: Abstract; Methods (selection of case studies, analytic plan); Case analysis (three cases); Findings and analysis (Table 1)
fields.exact_location: Methods; Case Analysis; Findings and Analysis (Table 1)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative analysis of three purposively selected tribal water-quality cases (Apsaalooke, Anishinaabe, Hoopa Valley) using Nutbeam's literacy typology; partnerships, skills and the ability to navigate laws and regulations are the recurring themes; documentary sources, no respondent data; read in full text 2026-10-04.
